q: How much of the paper's headline 99.9% accuracy is an artifact of the synthetic-read self-consistency loop (art-illumina reads from complete genome + Shovill assembly + AMRFinderPlus vs. AMRFinderPlus on the same complete genome) rather than a real-world performance number, and what is the *irreducible* WGS-vs-truth error when the synthetic-read closed loop is replaced with an orthogonal ground truth (long-read + phenotype + PCR + Sanger)?
basis: The paper's 133215-allele denominator (which drives the 99.9%/97.5%/100% numbers) comes from art-illumina reads generated from the SAME reference genomes that AMRFinderPlus scores as the 'gold standard'. Any error introduced by BLASTx / HMM / database curation is invisible in this design; only errors introduced by fragmentation + de novo re-assembly are testable. This is a well-defined circularity: abritAMR-of-synthetic-reads-from-G is being compared to AMRFinderPlus-on-G, where abritAMR IS AMRFinderPlus plus post-processing. Our replication confirmed the numeric agreement but did not resolve the circularity: our LOD re-pass at 40-150X showed 100% recall (41/41) with wgsim+SPAdes+AMRFinderPlus, which is arguably even MORE circular than the paper. The paper's PCR panel (n=1184) partially breaks this loop but is restricted to ~14 genes (CPE/ESBL/van/mec), and Sanger sequencing (n=356 alleles) further tightens it only for the carbapenemase-allele problem. The scaling of 'true' WGS-vs-truth accuracy across the full 415-allele × 43-subclass space is therefore unknown.
next_steps: (1) Build a hybrid ground-truth panel of ~50 isolates with (a) matched Illumina short reads, (b) PacBio HiFi or ONT R10 long reads assembled to closed circular genomes, (c) phenotypic AST, and (d) PCR for all 415 alleles where primers exist. (2) Score abritAMR, ResFinder 4.6, and CARD-RGI 6 on both the short-read-assembled and long-read-assembled inputs; the paired difference isolates the assembly/short-read error component from the tool+database component. (3) Report accuracy per antimicrobial class stratified by ground-truth source, and compare against the paper's 99.9% headline. Expected result: overall accuracy drops several percentage points once orthogonal truth is enforced, and beta-lactam allele-level accuracy drops substantially. (4) Publish the panel as a versioned public benchmark (Zenodo DOI + accession list) so future tool releases can be scored against a stable, non-self-consistent target.

q: What is the real distribution of computational precision (repeatability & reproducibility) for AMR gene calling when the pipeline is stressed with the sources of variance that actually occur in production sequencing — mixed cultures, plasmid dropout, low-frequency variants, sequencing-run-to-run chemistry drift, and analyst re-runs across different HPC schedulers/OS/CPU architectures — rather than the paper's within/across-run replicate design on a curated n=13 panel that yielded a trivial 100%?
basis: The paper's precision claim (100% within-run and between-run for n=13 organisms) is an under-powered lower bound. Our re-pass at 80X coverage across 3 wgsim seeds on 2 genomes gave identical AMRFinder call sets (Jaccard = 1.00) — but this is precision under IDEALISED conditions (identical software, identical DB, identical error profile, identical assembler flags). The paper does not stress-test any of the real variance sources: (a) mixed cultures (a real-world contamination frequency in CPHM labs), (b) plasmid dropout (which the paper acknowledges but does not measure), (c) sub-clonal variants, (d) library prep chemistry batch effects, (e) HPC scheduler + BLAST heuristic non-determinism, (f) OS / CPU-architecture differences (ARM64 vs x86_64 SPAdes). Any of these could produce > 0 call disagreement in real deployment.
next_steps: (1) Design a 6-factor DOE precision study: {contamination level, plasmid load, coverage, library kit, HPC arch, DB version} × 5-8 isolates × 3 replicates. (2) Sequence a subset of clinical CPE isolates with deliberate co-culture (e.g. 90/10 E. coli / K. pneumoniae) at 40X/80X/120X and quantify call-set disagreement. (3) Run identical FASTQs through the pipeline on x86_64 (Intel + AMD) and ARM64 (M-series Mac, Ampere) and quantify call divergence introduced by non-deterministic BLAST tie-breaks. (4) Report a *distribution* of Jaccard, not a point estimate; recommend a minimum acceptable Jaccard threshold for ISO 15189 accreditation.

q: For non-Salmonella species, what is the *quantitative* genotype → phenotype accuracy of abritAMR-style AMR gene detection, and can the Salmonella-only inferred-antibiogram module (n=864 isolates, 13 antimicrobials, single Australian lab, 2018-2019) generalise to Klebsiella pneumoniae, Escherichia coli, Acinetobacter baumannii, Enterococcus faecium, and Staphylococcus aureus — the pathogens where clinical decision support would actually matter?
basis: The paper's inferred-antibiogram is validated ONLY for Salmonella spp. and explicitly deferred for other species as future work. The 98.9% overall accuracy is driven by 11/13 antimicrobials being ≥98% concordant; the two failure classes (streptomycin 95.5%, ciprofloxacin 96.8%) are already the well-known genotype-phenotype trouble spots. The 5 critical AMR gene classes (carbapenemase, MBL, ESBL, mcr, vanA/B, mecA) that the paper claims 99.9% accuracy for are GENE-DETECTION metrics, not phenotype-prediction metrics; those two things are conflated in the paper's discussion. In actual CPHM practice, clinicians want a predicted antibiogram for a patient's isolate, which is a much harder problem than 'is the gene present'. The paper simply does not test this for anything except Salmonella. Our replication cannot fix this because the source data does not exist.
next_steps: (1) Assemble a multi-species phenotype panel: 500-1000 isolates each of E. coli, K. pneumoniae, A. baumannii, E. faecium, S. aureus, P. aeruginosa with paired MICs (broth microdilution CLSI 2024) and Illumina reads. Public candidates: NCBI PRJNA504926 (CDC AR Bank), ATCC Bacterial Genomics, PathogenWatch collections. (2) Build a species-specific weighting model for phenotype inference (Sherry's Salmonella logic 'zero mechanisms = S, one = I, ≥2 = R' is a simple additive model; it likely fails for species with strong efflux + regulator interactions like Pseudomonas). (3) Report per-species per-antimicrobial VME/ME/mA (very major error / major error / minor agreement) rates against FDA-CDRH ID/AST thresholds (VME ≤ 1.5%, ME ≤ 3%). (4) Identify which species/drug combinations are provably NOT accreditable to ISO 15189 with current gene-based inference alone (likely all Pseudomonas, most Enterobacter beta-lactams, most enterococcal aminoglycosides).

q: How do the 415-allele × 321-genome performance numbers change when the underlying AMRFinderPlus database evolves 3+ years forward (the paper used a 2022 DB; current is 2026-03-24.1) — specifically, do the paper's 5 residual discrepancies (3 FN / 2 FP) resolve with newer databases, do NEW discrepancies emerge from newly-curated alleles, and can a laboratory legally claim 'validated' status under ISO 15189 across arbitrary future database versions when the validation is anchored to a single frozen DB snapshot?
basis: The paper describes an 'abritAMR test suite' for re-verification after DB updates but does NOT report the results of any such re-verification, does not commit to a minimum accuracy delta that would trigger a full re-validation, and does not publish the test suite outputs across DB versions. Our replication used DB 2026-03-24.1 vs. the paper's ~2022 DB; source-data recomputation matched exactly (because source data is frozen), but ANY new run of AMRFinderPlus on the same genomes could produce different calls (new alleles added, thresholds tuned, sequence records corrected). The absence of a longitudinal DB-drift analysis is a real gap for any ISO 15189 lab: on paper the pipeline is 'validated', but the validated behaviour may drift silently between accreditation audits.
next_steps: (1) Replay AMRFinderPlus 3.x → 4.x on the paper's 321-genome synthetic dataset AND the PCR panel with 6-12 monthly DB snapshots (2022-01 through 2026-06). (2) For each DB version, compute (a) new calls, (b) removed calls, (c) allele-name changes (aac(6')-Ib → aac(6')-Ib' fam splits), (d) impact on the paper's 99.9% headline. (3) Fit a drift model and estimate: 'Given a validation on DB_v0, how many DB updates before the pipeline's operating characteristics fall outside a defensible re-verification envelope?' (4) Propose a formal 'validation-envelope' metric (e.g. per-class Jaccard between DB_v0 and DB_vN, weighted by clinical impact) that CPHM labs can compute against each new DB release to decide re-verify vs. re-validate. This directly addresses an operational gap in the ISO 15189 accreditation pathway that the paper opens but does not close.

q: What is the failure mode boundary between contig-break induced false negatives and true gene absence — specifically, how often are the 'FN' calls attributed to 'plasmid dropout in culture' or 'contig break within gene' actually failures of the abritAMR/AMRFinderPlus partial-hit handling logic itself, and can a coverage-aware, split-alignment-aware caller (e.g. a read-based caller such as ARIBA or KMA + ResFinder that never assembles) recover them?
basis: The paper attributes most residual FN calls (aac(6')-Ib family: 18 FN, aac(6')-Ib-cr5: 11 of those 18; some CTX-M / CMY families) to (a) contig-break fragmentation → gene split across two contigs → AMRFinderPlus HMM/BLASTx below threshold, and (b) plasmid dropout in culture. Distinguishing (a) from (b) is critical: (a) is a fixable software problem (better partial-hit merging, read-mapping-based rescue, long-read confirmation), (b) is a wet-lab problem (culture conditions) and non-fixable in silico. The paper does not quantify the split. Our replication also does not quantify it, because we used complete reference genomes and skipped the assembly step where these errors occur. This gap directly limits how much residual FN rate is 'fixable' vs. 'irreducible'.
next_steps: (1) Take the paper's 88 discrepant alleles (32 aminoglycoside FN, 18 aac(6')-Ib, etc. — accessions in Supp Data 3) and re-run with 3 orthogonal callers: (a) abritAMR/AMRFinderPlus on Shovill assembly (paper baseline), (b) ARIBA on raw reads (no assembly), (c) KMA + ResFinder on raw reads. (2) For each FN, classify: 'recovered by read-based caller' = software-fixable / 'not recovered by any caller' = plasmid dropout OR true absence / 'partial hit present in assembly but below AMRFinderPlus threshold' = threshold-tunable. (3) If a substantial fraction (e.g. > 30%) is software-fixable, propose a two-stage pipeline (assembly-based primary + read-based rescue) and quantify the accuracy lift; this could push the paper's 99.9% to ~99.99% and materially change the ISO 15189 case. (4) For the plasmid-dropout subset, sequence a matched pair of colony-picks per isolate to directly measure plasmid loss rate in overnight culture; publish as a baseline 'culture-loss floor' for the field.
